title: Emergency patch routing and LTS backport matrix
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Problem: We currently lack a concise decision matrix and lightweight playbook for determining how to route emergency fixes across channels (hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and LTS branches. That ambiguity slows time-to-fix and increases blast radius during incidents.

Goal: Produce a single-page emergency patch routing guide + backport matrix that: (1) defines severity criteria tied to concrete actions and SLAs, (2) specifies patch branch naming and cherry-pick/backport rules for semantic versioning and LTS channels, (3) enumerates verification gating (automated + manual), and (4) supplies templates for PRs, release notes, and postmortem tags.

Scope: Applies to rollback/hotfix flows across all Redwood deployments (hosted, dedicated, private). Excludes non-production experiments and changes that are purely config with no user-facing impact (those follow infra-config checklist).
acceptance_criteria: A one-page decision matrix mapping severity -> routing action -> SLA (TTx) exists in Docs and is referenced by on-call runbook.
Clear branch naming and backport rules documented and enforced by CI scripts that prevent accidental direct pushes to LTS branches.
Templates for emergency PR, cherry-pick commit message, and release note snippets are added to repository CONTRIBUTING.md.
At least two simulated drills performed during the cycle: a rollback drill and a cross-branch backport drill, with recorded outcomes.
Security review checkbox present for any fix touching auth/KMS/crypto paths before canary rollout.
decisions: Severity matrix will be discrete (S0, S1, S2, S3) with S0 requiring immediate pager and S1 requiring on-call within 1 hour.
All LTS branches are protected: direct pushes disabled; backports must come via cherry-pick PRs named 'cherry-pick: <orig-pr> -> <branch>'.
For hosted API customer-facing regressions affecting >=1% of requests, default routing is fast-track to runtime hotpatch on release/vX.y.z and simultaneous backport to LTS channels if applicable.
Private deployments get optional fast-path only when customer explicitly opts-in via Dedicated SLA addendum; otherwise, we provide a signed patch bundle and step-by-step upgrade runbook.
severity_criteria: S0: Security-critical remote code execution or encryption key compromise. Action: immediate page, block deployments, produce signed hotfix bundle. SLA: 4 hours to mitigation.

S1: Customer-facing data loss, major correctness regression affecting >=1% active sessions or major API reliability regression (p95 token latency >2x SLO). Action: page + targeted hotpatch. SLA: 24 hours to stable patch rollout.
S2: Significant regression with limited scope (single endpoint, single region). Action: ticket and expedited patch window during business hours. SLA: 3-7 days depending on testing burden.
S3: Minor behavioral/regression not impacting correctness or availability. Action: standard release cycle; no emergency backport. SLA: backlog grooming.
branch_strategy: Primary branches: main -> daily integration; release/vX.Y -> short-lived release branches; lts/YEAR-MAJOR -> LTS channels (eg lts/2025-1).
Patch branches: release/vX.Y/patches -> used for contiguous patch builds before creating release tags (eg release/v1.19/patches).
LTS patch branch naming: lts/<year>-<major>-patch/<YYYYMMDD>-<ticket>. Example: lts/2025-1-patch/20260310-ENG-20134.
Cherry-pick convention: 'cherry-pick(<orig-branch>, <orig-commit>): <short-desc> --backport-to: <target-branches>'. PR title enforced by CI template.
backport_policy: Backport targets: Any fix merged to main that is a security fix or S0/S1 regression MUST be backported to all active LTS branches that include affected code paths.
Scope selection: Backport only the minimal commits required to fix the issue; avoid feature commits or large refactors during backport PRs.
Automated checks: backport PRs must pass a 'minimal smoke' CI job that runs critical e2e scenarios scoped to the LTS surface area.
Approval flow: Backport PRs to LTS require at least two approvers: one from Infra/Runtime and one from Security if security_review_required=true.
testing_requirements: Canary matrix: every hotfix must run a canary suite against a small traffic slice for 2 hours with zero regression on defined canary metrics (error rate, p95 lat, token correctness).
Smoke tests: LTS backports run a trimmed smoke pipeline (startup, basic generation, KV cache stability) before merge.
Roll-forward tests: if a rollback was executed, the roll-forward path must be validated by running the full integration suite in a staging environment before re-deploy.
rollout_gates: Gate 0 (pre-merge): CI green on unit + lint + backport smoke job.
Gate 1 (canary): 2-hour canary with traffic targeting small subset (~0.5-2%) and watchlist for key metrics. Auto-rollback threshold defined per metric.
Gate 2 (regional rollout): expand to affected regions after 24h of stable canary.
Gate 3 (global): full rollout with monitoring alerts and post-deploy checklist items completed.
runbook_snippets: Emergency PR template: include 'S<severity>' badge, affected services, minimal repro, mitigation steps, and 'backport targets' line.
Rollback quick steps: 1) Identify faulty release tag; 2) Trigger 'release-rollback' job with tag; 3) Notify customers & update status page; 4) Open postmortem ticket and assign owner.
Hotfix delivery for Private: generate signed-patch.tar.gz, publish to secure S3 URL with short-lived credentials, and publish step-by-step upgrade instructions for customer ops.
operational_notes: CI enforcement: add 'backport-template' and 'cherry-pick' linter to PR checks to enforce naming and metadata fields.
Automation: create a lightweight 'backport-helper' GitHub Action that can open cherry-pick PRs and populate required labels and reviewers.
Monitoring: add a 'hotfix-rollout' dashboard in Console showing canary success/failure for ongoing emergency patches.
